messages:
michelle: Quick decision: for first-run "starter projects" should we use a large carousel banner on the console home or a compact horizontal rail inside the workspace card? pros/cons?
harry: carousel = high visibility, better for marketing-driven signups. rail = lower noise and keeps workspace-focused.
anita: accessibility point: carousel must have proper pause/prev/next controls and not auto-advance. each card needs keyboard focus and clear aria-label.
sam: analytics: carousel might spike clicks but also complaints if it obscures main CTA. rail probably has steadier conversion.
michelle: copy idea for carousel header: "Jumpstart with starter projects" vs rail header: "Starter projects". shorter wins for localization.
harry: runtime UX: cards should show estimated setup time ("~10s") so users know cost. also primary CTA = "Run" not "Try".
anita: a11y nit: badges must not rely on color. include text like "Ready"/"Requires API key" and ensure 4.5:1 contrast for labels.
sam: implementation note: preload card metadata only; full sample downloads on Run. feature flag rollout recommended.
design-bot: Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/zzz/starter-carousel-vs-rail (preview).
michelle: decision leaning: rail for returning users + carousel only for brand-new accounts in first session. toggle via server flag.
harry: agree. add a small "hide for session" control and a permanent "don't show again" setting.
anita: keyboard flow: focus order must not jump when carousel changes; prefer manual nav. announce card changes to SR when user navigates.
sam: metrics to track: card click-through, run-to-completion, and dismiss rate. target increase in time-to-first-run.
michelle: great. i'll draft spec that ships carousel to 100% new accounts for 1 week, then measure; rail becomes default for all others. PR incoming with Figma links."
